Datasheet fisher-et-d100022x012, pages [20, 21, 14, 15, 13, 18, 5, 12]:
The datasheet lists several materials for the valve-plug seals, with different temperature ranges. The ranges below are the listed material limits; the PTFE/graphite option’s upper limit depends on whether service is oxidizing. [p. 20]

- **Two-piece valve-plug seal:** Carbon-filled PTFE, **−73 to 232 °C (−100 to 450 °F)**; ethylene-propylene, **−40 to 232 °C (−40 to 450 °F)**; fluorocarbon, **−18 to 204 °C (0 to 400 °F)**; or nitrile, **−40 to 71 °C (−40 to 160 °F)** for air and hydrocarbons, or up to **82 °C (180 °F)** for other compatible fluids. These two-piece seals are standard for NPS 1–6 valves except those with Cavitrol III cages. The datasheet notes that ethylene-propylene cannot be used with petroleum-based fluids or other hydrocarbons; fluorocarbon is not for steam or ammonia and is not recommended for water above **82 °C (180 °F)**; nitrile cannot be used with fire-resistant hydraulic oils. [p. 20]
- **Spring-loaded valve-plug seal:** PTFE with an N10276 spring, **−73 to 232 °C (−100 to 450 °F)**. This is standard for NPS 8 valves and NPS 1–6 valves with Cavitrol III cages, and optional for NPS 1–6 valves with other cages. [p. 20]
- **PTFE/graphite with an R30003 spring:** **−73 to 316 °C (−100 to 600 °F)** when used with PEEK anti-extrusion rings; for oxidizing service, the maximum is **260 °C (500 °F)**. PEEK is the listed anti-extrusion-ring material; the table says it is “not limiting” for temperature. [p. 20]
- **PTFE V-ring:** **−40 to 232 °C (−40 to 450 °F)**. [p. 20]

Table 14 also lists spring-loaded seal components made of stainless steels, but says these materials are “not limiting factors” for temperature rather than giving them a temperature range. It notes that some parts are not used with ports **137 mm (7 in.) or larger**. [p. 20]
